themes.name: exporter-two-views-many-and-one
themes.title: Valkey metrics from two exporters
themes.desc: A fanned deck of five identical small readout cards, one per Valkey node with its own memory, client and command bars, beside one large single card holding per-slot counters for the whole cluster with the hottest slot drawn in red, representing one readout per node from one exporter and a single cluster-wide readout from the other. The title "Valkey metrics from two exporters" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: A deck of per-node readout cards beside one cluster-wide card with per-slot counters
themes.useFor: Per-pod series versus per-slot series, exporter choice
themes.caption: Metrics from two exporters

themes.name: keyspace-gui-safe-refusal
themes.title: Valkey server-side read-only
themes.desc: Four blue command lanes running in from the left, crossing a tall pale boundary bar and carrying on towards the white Valkey hexagon mark on the far side, and one much thicker red lane that reaches the same boundary, turns back on itself and returns the way it came, representing a write refused by the server rather than by a setting in the client. The title "Valkey server-side read-only" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: Read lanes crossing the server's boundary, one write turned back at it
themes.useFor: ACL users, read-only access, NOPERM, server-side authorisation
themes.caption: Server-side read-only

themes.name: keyspace-gui-safe-grant
themes.title: Valkey read-only ACL user
themes.desc: A field of forty-eight pale command pills laid out on an even grid, with sixteen of them lit green inside a rounded green boundary and three of those green pills struck through with a red line, representing a user granted the read commands as a category with the dangerous ones taken back out of the same grant. The title "Valkey read-only ACL user" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: A grid of commands with one block granted and the dangerous ones struck out inside it
themes.useFor: ACL grants, command categories, least privilege
themes.caption: Read-only ACL user

themes.name: keyspace-gui-safe-readout
themes.title: Valkey browsing a keyspace safely
themes.desc: The white Valkey hexagon mark on the left with four blue lanes fanning out of it into the left edge of a large client window, which holds four panels of read-only results: a row of counter bars, one large figure, a list of open connections and a list of slow commands with their durations, representing a graphical client that only renders what the server already publishes. The title "Valkey browsing a keyspace safely" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: A client window of four read-only panels, each fed by one read from the server
themes.useFor: GUI clients, INFO, CLIENT LIST, SLOWLOG, monitoring views
themes.caption: Browsing a keyspace safely

themes.name: commands-replace-lua-round-trips
themes.title: Valkey one round trip, not four
themes.desc: A caller on the left and a Valkey server drawn as the white hexagon mark on the right, with four thin purple messages crossing back and forth between them above, and one thick green call below carrying a pale condition chip that holds two unequal values, representing a conditional update that used to take an exchange of messages and now takes one command. The title "Valkey one round trip, not four" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: Four thin messages crossing between caller and server, one thick call below them carrying the condition
themes.useFor: Command options that collapse an exchange into one call
themes.caption: One round trip, not four

themes.name: commands-replace-lua-one-line
themes.title: Valkey one command, no script
themes.desc: A small quiet panel of ragged purple script lines above an arrow pointing down to one long bright command bar holding a run of pale words, with a green condition chip of two unequal values seated at the bar's end, representing a Lua script replaced by a single command with a condition option on it. The title "Valkey one command, no script" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: A quiet block of script lines giving way to one long command bar with a condition on its end
themes.useFor: New command options that replace a Lua script
themes.caption: One command, no script

themes.name: commands-replace-lua-condition-gate
themes.title: Valkey conditions inside the command
themes.desc: One thick blue command lane running into a large pale condition holding two unequal values, out of which a thick green branch carries the write up into a lit key block while a thin dim branch stops short at a blunt bar, representing a command that decides for itself whether its write lands. The title "Valkey conditions inside the command" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: A command lane running into a large condition, one branch carrying the write on and one stopping dead
themes.useFor: Conditional commands, `SET IFNE`, `EXEC IFEQ`, optimistic locking
themes.caption: Conditions inside the command

themes.name: ai-advisory-surge-sieve
themes.title: Valkey advisory surge
themes.desc: A wide flood of small identical report tokens falling and narrowing onto a row of evenly spaced light teeth, with only three red tokens through the gaps and resting on a short line below, representing far more vulnerability reports arriving than before and only a few of them being real advisories. The title "Valkey advisory surge" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: A flood of reports narrowing onto a toothed screen, three getting through in red
themes.useFor: Report volume, triage load, what counts as a vulnerability
themes.caption: Advisory surge

themes.name: ai-advisory-surge-reproducer
themes.title: Valkey security audits
themes.desc: A row of five identical candidate bug cards, four of them crossed out in red, the middle one lit green and dropping into a large panel holding four pale lines and a red one, representing self-run adversarial audits where a candidate only reaches a person once it comes with a reproducing crash. The title "Valkey security audits" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: Five candidate bugs, four struck out, the survivor dropping into its reproducer
themes.useFor: Adversarial audits, LLM-found bugs, verification before a human
themes.caption: Security audits

themes.name: ai-advisory-surge-backport-rails
themes.title: Valkey backported fixes
themes.desc: Five stacked version rails, each branching off the one above it and carrying a run of small blue commits, crossed by one bright green vertical line that places the same fix node on every rail at the same point, representing one security fix shipped to every supported version at once. The title "Valkey backported fixes" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: Five version rails with one fix node aligned on every one of them
themes.useFor: Backports, patch releases, shipping a fix to every supported version
themes.caption: Backported fixes

themes.name: fbtree-fanout-slab
themes.title: Valkey sorted sets in less memory
themes.desc: A scattered field of small separate member blocks, each carrying a short stack of purple pointer bars above it, over one wide green node along the bottom holding the same members as blue cells packed side by side and rising in score order, representing a sorted set index that stops spending one heap allocation per member. The title "Valkey sorted sets in less memory" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: A scattered field of pointer-topped member blocks over one wide node holding the same members packed in order
themes.useFor: Sorted sets on fbtree, index overhead, one allocation instead of many
themes.caption: Sorted sets in less memory

themes.name: fbtree-fanout-tiers
themes.title: Valkey sorted sets, fewer levels
themes.desc: A tall spindly purple tree of seven thin levels with a lookup route threading one node per level, beside a short broad green tree of one wide root node fanning into three leaf nodes of packed blue members, reached in two hops, representing a high-fanout B+ tree replacing a deep pointer structure. The title "Valkey sorted sets, fewer levels" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: A tall spindly seven-level tree beside a short broad two-level one, same members at the leaves
themes.useFor: High fanout, tree depth, fewer fetches per lookup
themes.caption: Sorted sets, fewer levels

themes.name: fbtree-fanout-leafwalk
themes.title: Valkey sorted set ranges in one walk
themes.desc: Seven separate member blocks at scattered heights joined by long purple arcs that climb out of each one to reach the next, above a chain of four green leaf nodes holding their members packed side by side with a single straight green arrow running the whole length of the chain, representing an ordered range read that no longer chases pointers. The title "Valkey sorted set ranges in one walk" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: Scattered blocks joined by climbing arcs above a chain of packed leaves with one straight run through it
themes.useFor: Ordered range reads, linked leaves, cache-friendly traversal
themes.caption: Sorted set ranges in one walk

themes.name: fake-in-process-enclosure
themes.title: Valkey inside the test process
themes.desc: One rounded process boundary containing a card of test lines on the left, three lanes running from it to the white Valkey hexagon mark on the right, and a short list of key and value pairs under that mark, with the only port on the wall drawn in dim purple and its lead ending in an unplugged connector outside, representing a Valkey server whose behaviour runs inside the test process. The title "Valkey inside the test process" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: One process wall holding the test, the server and its keys, with the port on that wall unplugged
themes.useFor: Test doubles, fakes, testing without a server or a container
themes.caption: Inside the test process

themes.name: fake-in-process-parity
themes.title: Valkey fake and real, same reply
themes.desc: Two identical columns of five reply capsules standing side by side, matched row for row in width and colour, with one pale caliper bracketing both from below; above the left column a dashed test card holds the white Valkey hexagon mark, and above the right the same mark sits in a solid server box with a port capsule and a connection running out of the frame, representing a fake inside the test process and a real Valkey server answering one assertion identically. The title "Valkey fake and real, same reply" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: Two identical reply columns under one caliper, one from a fake inside the test and one from a real server
themes.useFor: Compatibility between a fake and the server, differential testing
themes.caption: Fake and real, same reply

themes.name: fake-in-process-dropin
themes.title: Valkey test double, dropped in
themes.desc: A pale socket at the centre with two contacts, a green in-process server carrying the white Valkey hexagon mark seated in it on matching pins, a dim purple server carrying the same mark held out of the socket above with its network connection trailing off the frame, and a call arriving on a blue lane from the lower left, representing an in-memory test double dropped into the socket a real server used to fill. The title "Valkey test double, dropped in" is set on solid light blocks in the lower left.
themes.motif: A socket with an in-process server seated in it and the remote one held out, still trailing its network
themes.useFor: A drop-in test double, replacing a client with a fake
themes.caption: Test double, dropped in
